# `Q-18-13` — knitr Hook Replaced By The Document

> A chunk replaced a knitr hook, so that chunk and every later one keep knitr's finished markdown.

## What this means

knitr turns each chunk's code and results into markdown with a set of hooks
(`source`, `output`, `message`, `warning`, `error` and `plot`). Code such as

````markdown
```{r}
knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) paste0("> ", x))
```
````

replaces one of them for the rest of the document. Quarto records what each chunk produced
and presents it itself, and it cannot know what your hook did. So the chunk that replaced the
hook, and every chunk after it, keep the markdown knitr produced, and Quarto does not present
them from the recorded pieces.

The output is the same as knitr's. This is a note, not a problem: nothing needs fixing.

## How to change it

If you want Quarto to present those chunks itself, use the chunk options that do the same job
(for example `class.output`, `attr.source` or `collapse`) instead of replacing the hook.
